## Purpose and data notice

This is a portfolio demonstration of an R analysis workflow. It uses **fully synthetic data generated in this file**. It does not contain the original capstone dataset, student records, original report findings, or institutional attribution. The example is illustrative; results must not be interpreted as evidence about real students or schools.

## 1. Setup

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(effectsize)
library(car)

set.seed(2026)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
```

## 2. Create synthetic demonstration data

```{r synthetic-data}
n <- 120
survey_demo <- tibble(
  study_id = sprintf("DEMO%03d", seq_len(n)),
  migration_status = sample(c("Migrant", "Non-migrant"), n, replace = TRUE),
  sex = sample(c("Female", "Male"), n, replace = TRUE),
  age = sample(12:18, n, replace = TRUE),
  social_support = pmin(10, pmax(1, round(rnorm(n, 6, 2)))),
  sense_of_belonging = pmin(10, pmax(1, round(rnorm(n, 6, 2)))),
  study_hours = pmax(0, round(rnorm(n, 2.5, 1.1), 1))
)

academic_demo <- tibble(
  study_id = sample(survey_demo$study_id),
  exam_score = pmin(100, pmax(0, round(rnorm(n, 65, 12))))
)

# Example of basic structure checks
 dim(survey_demo)
 names(survey_demo)
 glimpse(survey_demo)
```

## 3. Merge and validate datasets

```{r merge-data}
analysis_data <- survey_demo %>%
  left_join(academic_demo, by = "study_id") %>%
  clean_names()

# Check key uniqueness and missingness
stopifnot(nrow(analysis_data) == n)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(analysis_data$study_id))

analysis_data %>%
  summarise(
    records = n(),
    missing_exam_scores = sum(is.na(exam_score)),
    unique_ids = n_distinct(study_id)
  )
```

## 4. Descriptive statistics

```{r descriptive}
analysis_data %>%
  summarise(
    mean_exam_score = mean(exam_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_exam_score = sd(exam_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_social_support = mean(social_support, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_study_hours = mean(study_hours, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

analysis_data %>%
  group_by(migration_status) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_exam_score = mean(exam_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_exam_score = sd(exam_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_social_support = mean(social_support, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## 5. Visualise distributions and group patterns

```{r plots, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
ggplot(analysis_data, aes(x = migration_status, y = exam_score)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Synthetic exam scores by migration group",
    x = "Demonstration group",
    y = "Exam score (0–100)"
  )
```

```{r support-plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
ggplot(analysis_data, aes(x = social_support, fill = migration_status)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Synthetic social-support scores",
    x = "Social-support score",
    y = "Number of demonstration records",
    fill = "Demonstration group"
  )
```

## 6. Group comparison and effect size

```{r t-test}
score_test <- t.test(exam_score ~ migration_status, data = analysis_data)
score_test

# Effect-size estimate for the group difference
effectsize::cohens_d(exam_score ~ migration_status, data = analysis_data)
```

## 7. Categorical association

```{r chi-square}
association_table <- table(analysis_data$migration_status, analysis_data$sex)
association_table

# Use cautiously when expected cell counts are small
chisq.test(association_table)
```

## 8. Correlation analysis

```{r correlation}
cor.test(
  analysis_data$social_support,
  analysis_data$exam_score,
  method = "spearman",
  exact = FALSE
)

numeric_data <- analysis_data %>%
  select(social_support, sense_of_belonging, study_hours, exam_score)
cor(numeric_data, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "spearman")
```

## 9. Interpretation and limitations

This document demonstrates common steps in a reproducible R workflow: creating and checking data, joining tables, summarising variables, visualising distributions, comparing groups, estimating effect size, testing categorical association, and exploring correlations.

Because the records are synthetic and randomly generated, any numbers or statistical test results produced when knitting this file are **not real research findings**. They should not be cited as evidence about migration, student well-being, or academic performance. A real analysis would also require documented variable definitions, a missing-data plan, appropriate checks of test assumptions, consideration of sampling design, and cautious interpretation of observational associations.

## Reproducibility note

The demonstration data are generated by code in this document, so no external spreadsheet or private dataset is needed. To reproduce the analysis, install the packages used above and knit this R Markdown file in RStudio.
